summary: We developed Mission Architect, a bilingual, offline pixel-art game in which players design, launch and operate complete space missions, from Earth orbit to landings at three lunar sites. In a research complex, players choose an objective and build a spacecraft from stages, engines, propellant, solar panels, batteries, antennas and science instruments. They then fly the mission: launch, orbit insertion, a transfer to the Moon with random events, and a hand-flown landing. The game addresses the challenge by linking mass, power, budget, data, communications and time on live dashboards, so every decision shows its ripple effect. Extra fuel adds speed but also weight, a better instrument raises science but drains power and overloads the antenna, and a longer mission yields more data at a higher cost and risk. A score, plain-language feedback, a guided tutorial, a formula calculator and three difficulty levels help players learn from both success and failure. This matters because students rarely get to experience how separate topics combine into one system.
details: Mission Architect is an offline, bilingual pixel-art game in which players plan, build and fly complete space missions. In a research complex, they choose a target, from Earth orbit to three lunar sites, and assemble a spacecraft from stages, engines, fuel, solar panels, batteries, antennas and science instruments. They then launch, enter orbit, travel to the Moon and land by hand. Real formulas for thrust-to-weight, the rocket equation, and power and data budgets drive six live dashboards, which show how each choice affects mass, power, budget, data, communications and time. After every flight, a scored report explains in plain language what went wrong and how to fix it. Players experience real engineering trade-offs safely and can retry quickly. There is a guided tutorial for new players and harder difficulties for more advanced ones. We want to give classrooms a free tool that builds systems thinking and an interest in space engineering. We built the game in Godot 4 with GDScript, combining AI-generated and hand-made pixel art. Creatively, it turns spreadsheets into play: you walk around the base, see your own rocket on the pad and steer the lander yourself. We balanced realism against simplicity, made sure no single design is perfect, and focused on accessibility, clear feedback and offline use.
